# LINT-075 native clock-series trial

These 11 schematics are synthetic Tooling fixtures generated by
`tests/design_lint_fixtures/clock_series_trial.py`. They contain no product
board, project contract, datasheet-derived requirement, or proprietary source.
The candidate result is only a review prompt; this trial does not establish
that a clock output needs a series resistor.

## Candidate provenance and boundary

- Repository: [`sabas0ba/kicad_skills`](https://github.com/sabas0ba/kicad_skills)
- Commit: `53d1af8bc550f60415b4b8e51a6d2d5924ada03f`
- Package: `eda-toolkit` 0.1.0; declared license: Apache-2.0
- Rule source SHA-256: `fd7427eb29ee099e3cb8868869be8e8b75ed7d72aeba07ad1b4fa5a8e8597d54`
- License SHA-256: `c71d239df91726fc519c6eb72d318ec65820627232b2f796219e87dcf35d0ab4`

The candidate selects `X` references or `Oscillator:` library symbols, then
examines the component references on an output net. It identifies a resistor
by reference prefix, does not inspect DNP state or value, and has no
project-authored topology map. The isolated trial environment and candidate
source remain outside this repository; the evaluation helper imports the
installed package only when run explicitly.

## Native source validation

KiCad CLI 10.0.6 exported all 11 schematics to native XML netlists. The
`native_kicad` pytest case compares every component pin's exported net with the
fixture's authored topology. All 11 ERC reports had zero errors. Each report
had two to five warnings for the intentionally unregistered `Synthetic`
symbol library; those warnings do not affect the connectivity assertions.

The earlier no-CLI fixture set remains unchanged and retains its original
hashes. Native ERC exposed that its `series-x-control.kicad_sch` is not a valid
native control: its `+3V3` label is on the same wire as X1's output and VDD
pin, and ERC reports two undriven power-input errors plus a multiple-net-name
warning. The expanded controls below were generated separately to keep that
historical record intact.

## Candidate results

The pinned `rule_clock_series_resistor` was run through the candidate's native
`ReviewContext` twice per fixture. All 11 targeted results repeated exactly
and matched the recorded observations. The first-party rule catalog has no
clock-series predicate; the test therefore compares the candidate heuristic
with synthetic intent, not with a first-party clock map.

| Fixture                              | Candidate result | Trial interpretation                                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `series-control.kicad_sch`           | Quiet            | 33 Ω series-path control                                                |
| `series-testpoint-control.kicad_sch` | Quiet            | Test point on source side; series path remains present                  |
| `direct-load-fault.kicad_sch`        | One finding      | Directly connected output and input                                     |
| `direct-testpoint-fault.kicad_sch`   | One finding      | Test point does not hide a direct load                                  |
| `direct-pull-fault.kicad_sch`        | One finding      | Shunt pull does not count as a series resistor                          |
| `wrong-net-fault.kicad_sch`          | One finding      | A resistor on a different clock net does not satisfy this output        |
| `bypass-fault.kicad_sch`             | One finding      | Direct connection bypasses the resistor                                 |
| `wrong-part-miss.kicad_sch`          | Quiet            | Miss: a ferrite bead with reference `R1` is treated as a resistor       |
| `dnp-series-miss.kicad_sch`          | Quiet            | Miss: the DNP resistor is accepted as fitted                            |
| `wrong-value-series-miss.kicad_sch`  | Quiet            | Miss: 1 MΩ is accepted because value is not checked                     |
| `direct-drive-control.kicad_sch`     | One finding      | Fixture-relative over-prompt on an explicitly allowed direct-drive path |

The five direct-load, pull, wrong-net, and bypass faults received prompts. The
candidate also prompted on the permitted direct-drive control and missed the
wrong-part, DNP, and wrong-value controls. The direct-drive result is a
fixture-relative over-prompt, not a field false-positive rate.

## Reproduction

Regenerate the fixtures with the Tooling development environment:

```sh
python -I -B tests/design_lint_fixtures/clock_series_trial.py
```

With KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 configured as the native test CLI, verify source
connectivity and ERC:

```sh
KICAD_GEOMETRY_TEST_CLI=/path/to/kicad-cli \
KICAD_GEOMETRY_TEST_VERSION=10.0.6 \
python -I -B -m pytest -q tests/test_design_lint_clock_series_trial.py
```

For the candidate trial, use a separate Python 3.11 environment, install its
pinned setuptools 83.0.0 backend and the public checkout at the commit above,
then run:

```sh
KICAD_CLI=/path/to/kicad-cli \
python -I tests/design_lint_fixtures/clock_series_candidate_eval.py
```

The trial installed the candidate with `--no-build-isolation --no-deps` to
exercise only this rule and the native KiCad adapter. It did not measure the
candidate's full dependency installation or Docker workflow.

## Disposition

The candidate contributes a narrow direct-load review hint, but it does not
honor project-specific direct-drive decisions and misses part identity,
population state, and value. Native KiCad validates these fixture netlists;
it does not determine whether a project needs a series element. Do not adopt a
generic first-party rule or runtime dependency from this trial. A future
project-authored path contract should be evaluated separately against exact
pins, a fitted resistor identity, and a reviewed value range. Part-specific
applicability, reviewer effort, the candidate's complete install flow, and
comparison with a first-party clock map remain unmeasured.
